En 1957, l'article « B2FH » de Margaret: In 1957, the "B2FH" paper by Margaret and Geoffrey Burbidge, William Fowler and Fred Hoyle explained how stars make elements heavier than iron by capturing neutrons.
La Polaire n'a pas toujours indiqué le n: Polaris has not always marked the north: because of the precession of Earth's axis, the celestial pole was close to the star Thuban around 2750 BC. Polaris will be closest to it shortly after 2100.
Dans l'Égypte ancienne, le premier lever: In ancient Egypt, the first rising of Sirius before dawn announced the Nile flood. In 1844, Bessel guessed it had an unseen companion; Alvan Clark saw it on 31 January 1862.
En 1930, à 19 ans, sur le bateau qui l'e: In 1930, aged 19, on the ship taking him from India to England, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar calculated the maximum mass of a white dwarf, about 1.44 Suns. Eddington mocked him publicly in 1935; he received the Nobel Prize in 1983.
Ptolémée comptait 48 constellations. Les: Ptolemy counted 48 constellations. The boundaries of today's 88 constellations were drawn by the Belgian Eugène Delporte, adopted by the International Astronomical Union in 1928 and published in 1930.
Le modèle de Kepler s'écartait de 8 minu: Kepler's model was 8 minutes of arc off Tycho's measurements of Mars, more than Tycho's error. "These eight minutes alone", he wrote, would lead to a reform of astronomy.
Cette « loi des aires » est publiée avec: This "law of areas" was published together with the first law in 1609 in Astronomia nova. The third law only came in 1619, in The Harmony of the World.
Newton a imaginé un boulet tiré du haut: Newton imagined a cannonball fired from the top of a very high mountain, "with no air about the earth": fast enough, it falls without ever reaching the ground. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World, published in 1728.
Newton a répondu par une expérience de p: Newton answered with a thought experiment: a cannonball fired from a very high mountain, fast enough, keeps falling without reaching the ground. The Moon does the same. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World (1728).
Pythéas a relié les marées à la Lune ver: Pytheas linked the tides to the Moon around 325 BC, and Seleucus of Seleucia, in the 2nd century BC, made it their cause. Galileo got it wrong in 1632 by blaming the Earth's motions. Newton gave the first explanation by gravitation in the Principia, in 1687.
Le premier module de la Station, Zarya,: The Station's first module, Zarya, was launched on 20 November 1998. It has been continuously inhabited since 2 November 2000.
Herman Potočnik décrit cette orbite en 1: Herman Potočnik described this orbit in 1928, and Arthur C. Clarke popularised it in 1945 in Wireless World magazine, hence its nickname, the "Clarke orbit". The first geostationary satellite, Syncom 3, was launched in 1964.
Arago aurait dit que Le Verrier avait dé: Arago is said to have remarked that Le Verrier had discovered a planet "with the point of his pen". Encouraged by this success, Le Verrier proposed another planet in 1859, Vulcan, close to the Sun: it was never found.
En 1783, le pasteur anglais John Michell: In 1783, the English clergyman John Michell took this idea to its limit: a massive enough star would have an escape velocity greater than the speed of light. These "dark stars", published in 1784 in a letter to Cavendish, could be spotted through a companion.
Kepler publie cette troisième loi en 161: Kepler published this third law in 1619 in Harmonices Mundi, The Harmony of the World, ten years after the first two.
John Michell imagine dès 1783 des « étoi: As early as 1783, John Michell imagined "dark stars" whose light cannot escape; his idea was rediscovered in the 1970s. The first image of a black hole, M87*, was released by the Event Horizon Telescope on 10 April 2019, then that of Sagittarius A*, at the centre of our galaxy, on 12 May 2022.
Le nom vient du grec galaxías kýklos, le: The name comes from the Greek galaxías kýklos, the "milky circle": in the myth, some of Hera's milk spilled across the sky when she pushed the infant Heracles away. Galileo was the first, in 1610, to resolve this band into stars with his telescope.
Ce chiffre vient surtout du satellite eu: This figure comes mainly from the European Planck satellite, launched on 14 May 2009 and named after the physicist Max Planck. In 2013, its team announced an age of 13.798 billion years.
Hubble repère des céphéides dans la nébu: Hubble spotted Cepheids in the Andromeda Nebula with the Hooker telescope on Mount Wilson. The New York Times reported his discovery on 23 November 1924, and he presented it to astronomers on 1 January 1925, despite opposition from Harlow Shapley.
Doppler explique l'effet en 1842 et Fize: Doppler explained the effect in 1842 and Fizeau suggested in 1848 applying it to the lines of stars. In 1912, Vesto Slipher found that Andromeda is moving towards us; in 1929, Hubble linked the redshift of galaxies to their distance.
Le nom « Big Bang » vient d'un adversair: The name "Big Bang" came from an opponent of the theory: Fred Hoyle, who backed a steady-state universe, spoke of "this big bang idea" on BBC radio in March 1949. He later denied meaning it as an insult.
Ralph Alpher et Robert Herman le prédise: Ralph Alpher and Robert Herman predicted it as early as 1948, at about 5 K. Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson picked it up by chance at Bell Labs, first measured on 20 May 1964. Hearing the news, Robert Dicke, who was searching for it, said: "Boys, we've been scooped." Nobel Prize 1978.
La source radio Sagittarius A* est décou: The radio source Sagittarius A* was discovered in February 1974 by Bruce Balick and Robert Brown. By following the orbit of the star S2 around it for years, Reinhard Genzel and Andrea Ghez showed it is a giant black hole: Nobel Prize in Physics 2020.
Galilée est le premier, en 1610, à voir: Galileo was the first, in 1610, to see with his telescope that the milky band of the Milky Way is made of countless stars. Today their number is estimated at between 100 and 400 billion.
Le savant persan al-Soufi décrit Andromè: The Persian scholar al-Sufi described Andromeda around 964, in his Book of Fixed Stars, as a "small cloud": the oldest known mention of another galaxy. The collision, long predicted for 4 billion years from now, has been judged far less certain since a 2025 study.
Dès 1884, Lord Kelvin estimait que beauc: As early as 1884, Lord Kelvin reckoned that many of the Galaxy's stars, "perhaps a great majority of them", might be dark bodies. In 1906, Henri Poincaré took up his calculation and spoke of "matière obscure", dark matter.
Lemaître, prêtre catholique belge, publi: Lemaître, a Belgian Catholic priest, published his expanding universe in 1927 in the Annales de la Société scientifique de Bruxelles. Einstein told him: "Your calculations are correct, but your physics is abominable." In 2018, the International Astronomical Union renamed Hubble's law the "Hubble–Lemaître law".
La spirale d'une galaxie est vue pour la: A galaxy's spiral was first seen with the Leviathan of Parsonstown, Lord Rosse's 72-inch telescope built in Ireland in 1845: it revealed the shape of M51, the Whirlpool Galaxy, which Rosse drew.
Ptolémée en comptait déjà 48 dans l'Anti: Ptolemy already counted 48 in Antiquity; Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille added about a dozen in the southern sky around 1756. The boundaries of today's 88 constellations were drawn by Eugène Delporte, adopted by the IAU in 1928 and published in 1930.
En 1838, Friedrich Bessel mesure la para: In 1838, Friedrich Bessel measured the parallax of the star 61 Cygni and noted that its light takes 10.3 years to reach us. The word "light-year" appeared in 1851 in a German popular article by Otto Ule. Eddington found it "an inconvenient and irrelevant unit".
Polaris n'a pas toujours été l'étoile du: Polaris has not always been the North Star: because of precession, the celestial pole was near Thuban, in Draco, around 2750 BC. Polaris will be closest to it, about 0.45 degrees, soon after the year 2100.
Newton construit son télescope fin 1668,: Newton built his telescope in late 1668, with a mirror of speculum metal, an alloy of tin and copper. A second one, shown to the Royal Society at the end of 1671, was presented to King Charles II in January 1672; Newton was elected to the Royal Society that same year.
Halley propose en 1716 de mesurer cette: In 1716 Halley proposed measuring this distance using the transits of Venus across the Sun. Those of 1761 and 1769 sent expeditions all over the world, including James Cook's to Tahiti; Le Gentil travelled for over eight years to see them. Lalande derived 153 million km from them in 1771.
Léon Foucault rend la rotation de la Ter: Léon Foucault made the Earth's rotation visible in February 1851, with a pendulum hung in the Meridian room of the Paris Observatory. A few weeks later, he hung it from a 67-metre wire under the dome of the Panthéon.
Le télescope James Webb, mené par la NAS: The James Webb telescope, led by NASA with the European and Canadian agencies, was launched on 25 December 2021 by an Ariane 5 from Kourou. It is named after James E. Webb, NASA administrator from 1961 to 1968. Its first image was released on 11 July 2022.
En 1866, l'Italien Giovanni Schiaparelli: In 1866, the Italian Giovanni Schiaparelli discovered that meteor showers are linked to comets: the August Perseids follow the orbit of comet Swift–Tuttle. Some Catholics call them the "tears of Saint Lawrence".
Angelo Secchi classe les spectres des ét: Angelo Secchi classified the spectra of stars in the 1860s and 1870s. At Harvard, Williamina Fleming and then Annie Jump Cannon set up the order O, B, A, F, G, K, M, and Cecilia Payne later showed it is a temperature scale, from hottest to coolest.
Spoutnik 1 est lancé le 4 octobre 1957 d: Sputnik 1 was launched on 4 October 1957 from Tyuratam, today's Baikonur: a 58 cm, 83.6 kg sphere whose "beep, beep" could be heard on the radio. It burned up re-entering the atmosphere on 4 January 1958. In the United States it set off the "Sputnik crisis", the start of the space race.
Au décollage, le 12 avril 1961, Gagarine: At lift-off, on 12 April 1961, Gagarin said "Poyekhali!", "Let's go!". He made a single orbit of the Earth and ejected at 7 km altitude to land by parachute, which the USSR only admitted in 1971.
Newton pose la loi de l'action et de la: Newton set out the law of action and reaction in the Principia in 1687. Yet in 1920 The New York Times mocked Robert Goddard, claiming a rocket cannot move in a vacuum; it printed a correction on 17 July 1969, during the Apollo 11 flight. Goddard had launched the first liquid-fuelled rocket on 16 March 1926.
Dès le XVIIe siècle, Newton expliquait l: As early as the 17th century, Newton explained an orbit as a fall: his cannonball fired from a very high mountain, fast enough, falls without ever reaching the ground. The picture appeared in A Treatise of the System of the World (1728).
Valentina Terechkova, ouvrière du textil: Valentina Tereshkova, a textile worker and amateur skydiver, flew solo aboard Vostok 6 on 16 June 1963, under the call sign Chaika, "Seagull". She orbited the Earth 48 times in almost three days. No woman went to space again until Svetlana Savitskaya, in 1982.
Ils ont marché sur la Lune lors de six a: They walked on the Moon during six Apollo landings, between July 1969 and December 1972. The first, Neil Armstrong, spoke of "one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind"; the last to climb back into the module was Eugene Cernan.
Voyager 1 est lancée le 5 septembre 1977: Voyager 1 was launched on 5 September 1977. It carries a golden record prepared by a team including Carl Sagan, took the 1990 photo of Earth known as the Pale Blue Dot, and entered interstellar space on 25 August 2012, the first probe to do so.
John Glenn a demandé Katherine Johnson p: John Glenn asked for Katherine Johnson by name and refused to fly until she had personally rechecked the computers' calculations for his Friendship 7 flight. Barack Obama gave her the Presidential Medal of Freedom on 24 November 2015; the film Hidden Figures came out in December 2016.
Tsiolkovski, sourd depuis ses neuf ans a: Tsiolkovsky, deaf since the age of nine after scarlet fever, had been teaching in Kaluga since 1892. His article appeared in May 1903. In 1911 he wrote: "Earth is the cradle of humanity, but one cannot live in a cradle forever."
On a longtemps annoncé 108 minutes ; sel: The figure long given was 108 minutes; according to more recent sources, the Vostok 1 flight lasted 106 minutes. Gagarin made a single orbit of the Earth, then ejected at 7 km altitude, which the USSR concealed until 1971.
Perseverance se pose dans le cratère Jez: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on 18 February 2021; its name was suggested by Alexander Mather, a schoolboy, in a contest. On 19 April 2021, the small Ingenuity helicopter it carried made the first powered flight on another planet.
Cette vitesse vient du boulet de Newton: This speed goes back to Newton's cannonball: fired fast enough from a high mountain, it falls without ever reaching the ground. Newton described the experiment in A Treatise of the System of the World, published in 1728.
Michel Mayor et Didier Queloz annoncent: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced 51 Pegasi b on 6 October 1995, measured with the ELODIE spectrograph at the Haute-Provence Observatory. A giant planet so close to its star contradicted the theories. It was named Dimidium in 2015, and its discoverers received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2019.
Le premier transit d'exoplanète, celui d: The first exoplanet transit, that of HD 209458 b, was observed in 1999 by two teams led by David Charbonneau and Gregory Henry. The space telescopes CoRoT, Kepler (launched in March 2009) and then TESS (April 2018) made it their method.
C'est la méthode de la première exoplanè: This is the method behind the first exoplanet around a Sun-like star: in 1995, Mayor and Queloz measured 51 Pegasi b this way with the ELODIE spectrograph at the Haute-Provence Observatory.
Les toutes premières exoplanètes confirm: The very first confirmed exoplanets orbit a pulsar: Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail discovered them on 9 January 1992 with the Arecibo radio telescope, in Puerto Rico.
L'expression « zone habitable » apparaît: The phrase "habitable zone" may have appeared as early as 1913 with Edward Maunder; Hubertus Strughold spoke of an "ecosphere" in 1953 and Su-Shu Huang developed the modern idea in the 1950s and 1960s. The nickname "Goldilocks zone", neither too hot nor too cold, dates from the 1970s.
Frank Drake l'écrit en 1961 comme simple: Frank Drake wrote it in 1961 as a mere agenda for the Green Bank conference, the first scientific meeting on the search for extraterrestrial intelligence. The participants called themselves "The Order of the Dolphin". The year before, his Project Ozma had listened to two nearby stars and picked up nothing.
En 1950 à Los Alamos, en allant déjeuner: In 1950 at Los Alamos, walking to lunch with Emil Konopinski, Edward Teller and Herbert York, Fermi reportedly said: "But where is everybody?" Tsiolkovsky had already raised the question in the 1930s, and Michael Hart examined it in detail in 1975.
Le 15 août 1977, le radiotélescope Big E: On 15 August 1977, Ohio State University's Big Ear radio telescope picked up a 72-second signal. Going over the printouts, astronomer Jerry Ehman circled "6EQUJ5" and wrote "Wow!" in the margin. A 2024 study suggests instead a cold hydrogen cloud that suddenly brightened.
Europe est découverte par Galilée le 8 j: Europa was discovered by Galileo on 8 January 1610. The Galileo probe, orbiting Jupiter from 1995 to 2003, detected an induced magnetic field there that betrays a salty water ocean under the ice. The Europa Clipper mission left to explore it on 14 October 2024.
Les fausses alertes sont nombreuses : la: False alarms are common: the phosphine detected on Venus in 2020 and the dimethyl sulfide suspected on K2-18b in 2023 were both later given possible explanations without life.
L'étoile TRAPPIST-1 est découverte en 19: The star TRAPPIST-1 was discovered in 1999 by John Gizis. In 2016, the team of the Belgian Michaël Gillon, at the University of Liège, found planets around it with the TRAPPIST telescope at La Silla, Chile; in 2017, further analysis added more.
Proxima b est annoncée le 24 août 2016 p: Proxima b was announced on 24 August 2016 by the European Southern Observatory, after the Pale Red Dot campaign led by Anglada-Escudé's team.
Étudiant l'amas de Coma en 1933, Zwicky: Studying the Coma Cluster in 1933, Zwicky found far more mass than could be seen and called it "dunkle Materie", dark matter. The phrase already existed in French: Poincaré had spoken of "matière obscure" in 1906.
Vera Rubin travaillait avec Kent Ford, f: Vera Rubin worked with Kent Ford, an instrument-maker, and his image-tube spectrograph. Their 1970 paper dealt with the rotation of Andromeda. In 2019, the large LSST telescope was renamed the Vera C. Rubin Observatory.
L'idée de corps célestes invisibles est: The idea of invisible celestial bodies is old: in 1884, Lord Kelvin supposed that many of the Galaxy's stars might be dark, and Poincaré spoke of "matière obscure", dark matter, in 1906.
Les résultats finaux du satellite Planck: The final results of the Planck satellite, in 2018, give about 4.9% ordinary matter, 26.6% dark matter and 68.5% dark energy.
L'accélération de l'expansion est découv: The accelerating expansion was discovered in 1998 by two rival teams, the Supernova Cosmology Project and the High-Z Supernova Search Team, using distant type Ia supernovae. Three of their members were awarded the Nobel Prize.
Einstein montre en 1915 que la lumière d: In 1915 Einstein showed that light should be bent twice as much as Newton predicts. Eddington and Dyson checked it during the eclipse of 29 May 1919, at Sobral in Brazil and on Príncipe. Zwicky suggested galaxies as lenses in 1937; the first one was found in 1979.
Le nom MACHO a été forgé par l'astrophys: The name MACHO was coined by the astrophysicist Kim Griest. The big microlensing surveys did not find enough of them: the MACHO team claimed perhaps 20%, the EROS2 team did not confirm it, and the Hubble telescope showed that less than 1% of the halo is made of red dwarfs.
La NASA annonce le résultat le 21 août 2: NASA announced the result on 21 August 2006 under the title "NASA Finds Direct Proof of Dark Matter", based on Chandra X-ray images and the paper by Clowe and colleagues. Supporters of modified gravity (MOND) still dispute this reading.
Einstein introduit sa constante en 1917: Einstein introduced his constant in 1917 to get a static universe, then abandoned it after Hubble confirmed the expansion. That he called it his "biggest blunder" rests only on George Gamow: the attribution is still debated.
Planck est lancé le 14 mai 2009 avec l'o: Planck was launched on 14 May 2009 together with the Herschel observatory, on an Ariane 5 from French Guiana. It was switched off on 23 October 2013. Its first results, in 2013, gave 13.798 billion years.
Lemaître propose l'expansion en 1927, Hu: Lemaître proposed the expansion in 1927, and Hubble published the relation between redshift and distance in 1929. In 2018, after a 78% vote, the International Astronomical Union recommended calling it the "Hubble–Lemaître law".
